name: Copernicus Sentinel (Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem)
short: Free EU Sentinel radar and optical satellite imagery, usually online 1-4 hours after each pass.
summary: The EU's Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem serves new Sentinel-1 (C-band radar, works day and night through cloud), Sentinel-2 (13-band optical, 10 m best) and other Sentinel products free, via STAC, OData, S3, Sentinel Hub and openEO, with PUSH/PULL catalogue subscriptions and a public Traceability service whose traces carry signed product hashes.

tasks: find the newest Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 product over a place (STAC or OData search, keyless)
subscribe to new products matching an area and filter (PUSH or PULL, account needed)
download full products (token) or render a cropped image or index via the Sentinel Hub Process API
check a product's BLAKE3 hash against its signed Traceability trace

pricing.notes: Free for Copernicus General Users: 12 TB download per rolling 30 days (then slowed to 1 MB/s and 1 connection, not cut off), 4 concurrent connections; Sentinel Hub 10,000 requests and 10,000 processing units per month.

latency.typical: about 1 h (Sentinel-1 GRD) to about 3.5-4 h (Sentinel-2 L2A) after sensing
latency.notes: Measured on 2026-10-26 (UTC early 27th) by keyless STAC search: a Sentinel-1C GRD COG sensed 03:49:59Z was published 04:44:50Z (55 min); a Sentinel-2C L2A tile sensed 00:58:11Z was published 04:32-04:34Z (about 3 h 35 min). The Sentinel-1 mission page says marine monitoring services need data 'typically in less than 3 hours'. The next pass depends on orbit; there is no tasking.

coverage.notes: No country limit. Sentinel-2 systematically covers land between 56° S and 82.8° N, coastal waters to 20 km, islands over 100 km² and closed seas, not open ocean. Sentinel-1 follows its observation scenario; revisit depends on orbit and there is no tasking.

licensing.summary: Sentinel Data Legal Notice (EU law): free, full and open access; reproduction, distribution, communication to the public, and adaptation, modification and combination are permitted 'in so far as it is lawful'; credit 'Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]' (or 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]'). No warranty; rare limits for security, third-party rights or service disruption. Other portal content is non-commercial only, and the Terms say "ESA and T-Systems do not grant the right to resell or redistribute any information, documents, images or material" (portal-content context, not the Sentinel Legal Notice). Neither AI training nor resale is named, so both stay unstated.

human.unknown: No people capture the data; satellites operated for the EU by ESA.

application.unknown: No device or app attestation applies; satellites are operated for the EU by ESA. The signed Traceability record is a custody record, not attestation, and is listed under provenance.custody (STANDARD §3, 3.1).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Mission, satellite and instrument (MSI optical, C-SAR radar) are named in the product name and metadata. Instrument identity rests on product metadata; nothing signs it at the sensor.

time.method: Sensing start and end times in product name and metadata
time.unknown: Sensing time is in product metadata; not independently attested. The trace timestamp shows only when CDSE registered the product.

location.method: Footprint geometry and orbit in product metadata
location.unknown: Geolocation comes from product metadata and orbit data; not independently attested.

content.unknown: No manipulation detection. Integrity since CDSE registered the product can be checked against the signed Traceability record (provenance.custody), but that is not a capture-time seal: there is no C2PA hard binding.

corroboration.unknown: Not cross-checked by a third party.

custody.method: CDSE's public Traceability service keeps a trace per product: the event (CREATE at registration), a BLAKE3 hash of the product (per-file hashes on most products), the holder (origin cdse_csc@dataspace.copernicus.eu) and the time, signed RSA-SHA256 with an X.509 certificate for trace.dataspace.copernicus.eu. Anyone can fetch the trace without a login, re-hash a download and compare.
custody.unknown: One documented hop (ground segment registration to you), signed by CDSE itself, not an independent party; it shows the bytes match what CDSE registered, not what the sensor saw. The sampled trace is timestamped 2024-06-19 but its signing certificate (GeoTrust TLS RSA CA G1) was valid only 2023-05-16 to 2024-05-15, so a strict X.509 check at signing time fails; the hashes can still be recomputed. Whether the list of traces is append-only is not documented, and some traces carry only the product hash. Kept at claimed: the trace is signed by the operator itself and the sample's signing certificate had expired before the trace date, so a strict public check fails.

sources.claim: Traceability: signed traces of a product's lifecycle events let users verify authenticity and integrity
Sample trace: CREATE event, BLAKE3 product and file hashes, signature block (certificate expired 2024-05-15, trace 2024-06-19)

delivery.basis: Sentinel-1 mission page: near-real-time data 'typically in less than 3 hours'; measured publication lag 55 min (Sentinel-1 GRD) to about 3.6 h (Sentinel-2 L2A); subscriptions notify on each new product.

rate_limit.notes: Keyless STAC search. With a token: 240 per minute, bursts up to 10/s. Sentinel Hub 300 requests and 300 processing units per minute; downloads 4 connections at 20 MB/s; S3 2,000 requests per minute (Quotas page).

auth.how_to_get: STAC and OData catalogue search and Traceability lookups need no account.

Free CDSE account (register, verify e-mail); password grant with client cdse-public (add totp if 2FA is on) returns a bearer token valid 10 minutes plus a refresh token valid 60 minutes. Needed for OData download and subscriptions.
Sentinel Hub APIs: create an OAuth client (client ID and secret) in the Sentinel Hub dashboard under User Settings, then use the client_credentials grant.
S3 access to eodata.dataspace.copernicus.eu: generate an access key and secret key with an expiry date after logging in to the CDSE account.

endpoints.params: collections, bbox|intersects, datetime, filter, sortby, limit

endpoints.notes: Bearer token from the cdse-public password grant
Sentinel Hub Process API: cropped image or index for an area; Sentinel Hub OAuth client token
PULL subscription queue of new-product notifications; create with POST /odata/v1/Subscriptions and acknowledge with /Ack?$ackid=; bearer token; at most 2 running subscriptions per user
Keyless; signed trace with BLAKE3 product hash

api.rate_limits: STAC search 60 requests/min per IP keyless, 240/min with a token, bursts up to 10/s; Sentinel Hub 300 requests/min and 300 processing units/min; downloads 4 concurrent connections at 20 MB/s each; S3 2,000 requests/min; subscriptions 2 running (10 total) per user
api.notes: STAC, OData search and trace lookups are keyless; a key (token) is needed only to download products and for subscriptions. STAC moved to stac.opensearch.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1 (announced 2026-10-16); the old stac.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1 runs alongside until 2027-01-12, then is replaced. Free-text search now sorts by relevance by default, so send sortby=-datetime for newest first.

requester.checks: A free account with a verified e-mail and accepted terms is needed to download or subscribe; search needs none. One person or organisation must not use many accounts to bypass quotas.
requester.unknown: No identity check beyond e-mail is documented; nobody is sent to a place.

sources.claim: New STAC endpoint stac.opensearch.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1 (published 2026-10-16); old stac.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1 runs alongside until 12 January 2027, then is replaced; 60 requests/min per IP unauthenticated, 240/min with a token, bursts 10 requests/s; relevance-based default sort

Live trace (fetched 2026-10-26): hash_algorithm BLAKE3, product and per-file hashes, signature algorithm RSA-SHA256 with certificate

Keyless STAC search on the new host returned the newest Sentinel-2 L2A product with datetime, eo:cloud_cover, published and a self link (2026-10-28; Sentinel-1 checked on the old host 2026-10-26)
PUSH/PULL subscriptions, token required, Read/Ack endpoints, 2 running subscriptions per user
Sentinel Hub OAuth clients and client_credentials grant
Sentinel Hub Process API endpoint (example request)

Sentinel-2: 13 bands (four at 10 m), 290 km swath, systematic coverage of land 56° S to 82.8° N
